title: Chat answers from stale earlier turns over its fresh context ('only kestrel, atlas, and delta' when the context said 'Agents: none active')
repro: Have a conversation in which an earlier answer listed sessions
Wait until Home drops them, then ask 'tell the vibepet session to run its tests'
expected: the reply reflects the current context, or says the earlier list may be out of date
actual: the context was 'Agents: none active.' The reply said 'there's no session called "vibepet" anyway — only kestrel, atlas, and delta'. That came from the flattened history, which is appended after the live context with nothing marking it stale
truth: 02:08:00Z: vibepet idle 13 min, kestrel waiting / permission prompt, beacon waiting / input needed, atlas and delta idle

title: CH1: first token median 3.2 s (p95 7.0 s, n=14) because every message cold-spawns claude -p (process overhead median 1.06 s per send)
repro: Click Net, type a question, Enter; time Enter → first model text (page probe)
Repeat; wrap the binary to time each spawn
expected: first token ≤ 1.5 s (rubric 95), and B1.3 p50 ≤ 2.0 s / p95 ≤ 3.5 s on the login path
actual: F1: 2494 / 2208 / 2284 ms (median 2284). All 14 sends: median 3198, p90 4282, p95 6955 ms. Each send spawns a fresh claude: 906–1465 ms of process overhead outside the CLI's own duration_ms (median 1059), plus a median API time of 2079 ms
truth: engine = the user's Claude Code login, claude-sonnet-5 (from the CLI JSON); load 2.1-6.7

title: CH5: nothing streams: every reply appears whole after 2.2-7.0 s (0 incremental DOM updates in 14 replies) behind a fake 'reading the repo / thinking' ticker
repro: Send any message
Observe #msgs with a MutationObserver
actual: 1 DOM insert per reply, 0 updates after it. Before that, a canned ticker cycles every 1.8 s whatever is happening (it said 'thinking…' for the whole 90 s offline wait)

title: CH2/B1.5: an unavailable model costs a failed cold spawn (+1.5-1.7 s) on every send, silently falls back to claude-opus-5-5, and is never remembered
repro: Set the profile's model to an id this login can't use (here 'claude-unavailable-model-x')
Send two messages
expected: at most one extra round trip, the first time only, plus a note: '<model> isn't available on this login. Using <fallback> instead.'
actual: each send spawned with the bad model (failed after 1545 / 1665 ms: 'There's an issue with the selected model…'), then re-spawned on the CLI default. Answers came from claude-opus-5-5 with no note. First token 5090 / 4637 ms

title: CH4/B3.6: every chat send writes 0.9-1.8k tokens of prompt cache that is never read (cache_read 0 in 13/13 sends), roughly doubling cost per send
repro: Send 5+ messages in one conversation with the CLI JSON captured
Read usage.cache_read_input_tokens / cache_creation_input_tokens
expected: ≥ 50 % cache reads from turn 3 (stable prefix first, live context last)
actual: cache_read_input_tokens 0 on every send; cache_creation 928-1780 on every send over ~1k tokens. Cost $0.0024 for the one sub-1k prompt, $0.0046-0.0076 for the rest. The live context (with the clock) sits before the conversation, so no prefix repeats

title: CH6/B2.4: Esc while a reply is pending closes the panel instead of stopping it; the request runs on and the answer pops up as a 140-char truncated bubble
repro: Send 'what does beacon need from me?'
Press Esc while 'reading the repo…' shows
expected: Esc (or a stop button) cancels within 200 ms, keeps the partial text marked 'stopped', and leaves the panel open
actual: the panel closes at once; the claude process keeps running. 3.3 s later the reply appears as a speech bubble cut to 'There's no agent named beacon in what I can see — just kestr…'. There is no stop control anywhere

title: CH8/B2.2: markdown lists and links in replies render as raw text, and code blocks lose their language label

expected: lists and links rendered (with a copy button on the code block)
actual: '- [kestrel](https://vibepet.net) — working' shown verbatim. No <ul> or <a> in the DOM. The code block reads 'code', not 'bash'. Its copy button works

Quit the app
Relaunch with the same profile and click Net

Type /new and Enter; press ⌘N

title: CH15/CH16: offline and HTTP 429 both show 90 s of 'thinking…' then 'claude timed out'; the cause is never detected (on 429 the CLI was retrying every 23 s)
repro: Launch with ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9 and send a message
Launch with ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL pointing at a local server that returns 429 + retry-after: 23 + rate_limit_error JSON, and send
expected: offline: 'You're offline. I'll send this when you're back.' (queued). 429: 'Rate limited by Anthropic. Retrying in 23 s.' with a countdown and [Retry now]
actual: both: 'thinking…' for 90.0 s (90036 / 90068 ms), then 'That didn't work: claude timed out'. On 429 the server log shows POST /v1/messages at +0.6, +23.6, +46.6 and +69.7 s. The app's 90 s kill hid it; the CLI wrote nothing to stdout
truth: fault injection at the network boundary

title: CH14/B4.2: chat errors are raw strings with no action, and the failed message can't be retried (composer cleared)
repro: Launch with an invalid ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and send; or trigger the offline case above
expected: '<what happened>. <what to do>' plus one primary action (e.g. 'That API key was rejected… [Paste key]'), with the text kept in the composer or as a retryable message
actual: 'That didn't work: API key is invalid.' / 'That didn't work: invalid x-api-key' / 'That didn't work: claude timed out'. No button; the key form is not offered; the composer is empty; the user bubble has no retry

actual: 'Key saved. Chat will use it.' (state.engine = 'key'). The next send fails 'That didn't work: invalid x-api-key' and nothing points back to the key form

title: CH19: a message sent while a reply is pending is silently dropped and the composer cleared

While 'reading the repo…' shows, type 'and after that one?' and press Enter

title: CH26/B5.3: the user can't see what chat was told: it answered from 'Agents: none active' while 5 sessions were alive, and nothing on screen says so
repro: Ask any question while sessions are hidden from Home
Compare the reply with the context the app sent (wrapper capture)
expected: a 'What Net sees' disclosure with the exact context and its token count
actual: the footer says only 'Via Claude Code · sends message + repo context'. There is no way to see 'Agents: none active.' or why an answer is wrong

title: CH32/CH34/CH35: the composer's keyboard flow stops at Enter/Esc: Shift+Enter submits (single-line input); ↑, ⌘N, ⌘K, ⌘1 and ⌘⇧C do nothing
repro: Type /today then Shift+Enter
In an empty composer press ↑, ⌘N, ⌘K, ⌘1
With a code block in the last reply press ⌘⇧C
expected: ⇧↵ newline (growing textarea), ↑ edits the last message, ⌘N new chat, ⌘K palette, ⌘1-9 act on the Nth session, ⌘⇧C copies the last code block
actual: Shift+Enter posted the /today note; the composer is an <input>. All the others: no change, and no clipboard write

why: Intermittent: 2 of 5 answers given after the context changed used earlier turns over the fresh context. At 02:36:37 the context said 'Agents: none active.' and the reply said 'only the vibepet repo and its single idle agent are visible in this context'. That idle agent came from turns 1-2. At 02:37, with the same context: 'no active agents right now, just vibepet sitting idle'. My two dedicated attempts ('tell the vibepet session to run its tests' 02:35:22, 'which of my sessions are idle right now?' 02:35:54) answered from the fresh context. The flattened history follows the live context with no timestamps and nothing marking older turns as superseded. Here the stale fact happened to be truer than the context, because of r1-S2-02.

Enter → first visible text: median 3305 ms, max 3570 ms (n=9, load 1.38-3.67), against B1.3 p50 ≤ 2.0 s and the rubric's ≤ 1.5 s. Each send spawns a fresh claude -p. Spawn → stdout closed, minus the CLI's own duration_ms, is a median 990 ms (n=7). API time adds a median 1988 ms, and nothing shows until the whole answer exists (r1-S2-08).

0 DOM mutations after the reply node in 10/10 measured replies (MutationObserver on #msgs). The reply is inserted whole after 2.0-3.6 s. Before that a fixed ticker runs: 'reading the repo' (0 ms) → 'checking your agents' (1854 ms) → 'thinking', unrelated to progress. It read 'thinking' at 6 s of both 90 s fault hangs.

With the profile model set to 'claude-unavailable-model-x', I sent two messages. Each first spawned with that model: is_error 'There's an issue with the selected model…', 1449 / 1299 ms wall. Each was then re-spawned without --model. Both answers came from claude-opus-5-5 with no note in chat, and send 2 repeated the failed spawn. First text 6023 / 4849 ms (load 3.7-3.9).

In 14/14 sonnet sends cache_read_input_tokens was 0 and cache_creation was 1135-1864 tokens (all ephemeral_1h), including turns 3-11 of one conversation. The CLI's costUSD implies $4/MTok for those writes and $10/MTok for output. At the 2x 1h-write rate an uncached prompt costs about half on input (turn 1: $0.0056 vs ~$0.0030), so 'roughly doubling' holds. Correction to the cause: the clock's position doesn't matter. Each send is a new process with the whole chat flattened into one stdin message, so no cacheable prefix ever repeats (the ~250-token system prompt is under the cache minimum).

I sent a question and pressed Esc 0.5 s later. #chat hid at once and the composer cleared, but the claude process (pid 97470) kept running. 4.3 s later the reply appeared as a speech bubble cut at 140 of its 517 chars ('…against a live fleet of agent sessions f'). There is no stop control.

The raw reply '- [kestrel](https://vibepet.net)
- **beacon**

```bash
./deploy.sh --dry-run
```' rendered its list and link as literal text: 0 <ul>/<li>, 0 <a>. Bold and the code block render, and the copy button exists. The block's label is the CSS constant 'code': the fence regex strips 'bash'.

While a reply was pending I wheeled #msgs up to scrollTop 0, 461 px above the bottom. When the reply landed, scrollTop jumped to 480 (the reply's first line, at the bottom). No pill or 'new' marker appeared.

24 bubbles, then quit, relaunch with the same userData and click Net: 0 messages, Quick asks back, scrollTop 0. state.json has no chat or history key, and a grep of the whole profile for a sent question found nothing.

'/new' → 'Unknown command /new. Type / to see them.' ⌘N in an empty composer changed nothing (message count 23 before and after). The Quick asks (#chips) are display:none once the chat has a message, and they came back only after an app restart.

Two fault runs in parallel (load 8.1): ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9, and a local 429 server sending retry-after 23. Both showed 'thinking' at 6 s, then 'That didn't work: claude timed out' at 90107 / 90063 ms. The 429 server got POST /v1/messages at +0.8, +23.9, +46.9 and +69.9 s after spawn, so the CLI was retrying on schedule. stdout stayed empty and stderr is discarded, so the app never learns the cause.

Offline, 429 and a rejected key all end as a raw 'That didn't work: <string>' bubble ('claude timed out' x2, 'invalid x-api-key'). There is no action button and the key form isn't re-offered after the key error. The composer is empty (cleared on submit), the user bubble has no retry, and its turn is popped from history.

claude not findable (VIBEPET_CLAUDE_BIN=/nonexistent, HOME → an empty dir, launchd PATH) and no key: chatVia() was null. The key form showed with focus in its password field, and #chatForm, #msgs and #chips were display:none. '/today' typed into the key field. The header read 'kestrel/main · api key' though no key existed. The copy offers only pasting a key; there is no install or login path.

Same no-engine profile: "what's my agent doing?" typed into the auto-focused key field plus Enter gave 'Key saved. Chat will use it.' (state.engine 'key', keyEnc set). The next composer send failed in 162 ms with 'That didn't work: invalid x-api-key', and nothing points back to the key form.

'which session needs me first?' + Enter. At +852 ms, with 'reading the repo' showing, I typed 'and after that one?' + Enter. The composer emptied at +858 ms and no user bubble was added. The wrapper logged 1 spawn, and stdin ends at the first question. No notice.

Nothing on screen shows what chat was sent. The wrong answers above came from 'Agents: none active.' while 5 sessions were alive, and nothing disclosed it. Correction: the footer the driver quotes isn't visible either. #chatNote has the hidden attribute and nothing unhides it (dropped in 1a7a276), so only the header 'vibepet/main · claude code' shows.

'/today' + Shift+Enter posted the day-book note, because the composer is an <input>. In an empty composer, ↑, ⌘N, ⌘K and ⌘1 changed nothing: message count, input and panel stayed the same. ⌘⇧C with a code block in an earlier reply wrote nothing to the clipboard, which I had instrumented to record only.
